title: Marbury v. Madison (1803)
summary: The Supreme Court articulated judicial review: courts may invalidate acts of Congress that conflict with the Constitution.

title: Brown v. Board of Education (1954)
summary: Held that state laws establishing separate public schools for Black and white students were unconstitutional.
principle: Equal protection and desegregation in public education.

title: Miranda v. Arizona (1966)
summary: Required police to inform suspects of rights to counsel and against self-incrimination before custodial interrogation.
principle: Fifth and Sixth Amendment safeguards in custodial interrogation.

title: New York Times Co. v. Sullivan (1964)
summary: Constitutional limits on defamation suits by public officials; actual malice standard for speech about public figures.
principle: First Amendment protection for criticism of public officials.

title: Gideon v. Wainwright (1963)
summary: States must provide counsel to indigent defendants in felony cases under the Sixth Amendment.
principle: Right to appointed counsel in serious criminal prosecutions.

title: United States v. Nixon (1974)
summary: Executive privilege could not shield tape recordings from a criminal subpoena in a prosecution context.
principle: Limits on executive privilege and rule of law in investigations.

title: Obergefell v. Hodges (2015)
summary: Same-sex couples have a fundamental right to marry protected by the Due Process and Equal Protection Clauses.
principle: Marriage equality under federal constitutional guarantees.

title: Chevron U.S.A., Inc. v. NRDC (1984)
summary: Framework for courts reviewing agency interpretations of ambiguous statutes—often taught in admin law.
principle: Judicial deference to reasonable agency statutory interpretations (historical framework).
